name: Storm Ion Pro
laneMatch: Fresh medium and medium-long sport patterns
layoutTip: Benchmark around 50 x 4 x 30 to keep roll in front of you.
summary: Top sport-shot read ball with strong midlane and low overreaction at breakpoint.
cons: Can read too early on lower volume
Needs cleaner companion ball

name: Motiv Evoke Hysteria
laneMatch: Longer volumes where front-to-back blend is critical
bowlerMatch: Rev-dominant players needing traction with continuation
layoutTip: Stronger drilling keeps shape from floating too long.
summary: A heavy-read sport ball that still keeps enough continuation for tougher blocks.
cons: Requires speed control
Can be too much on shorter sports

name: Hammer Black Widow Urethane
laneMatch: Short sport and high-friction tournament surfaces
bowlerMatch: Higher rev players controlling pocket from outside
layoutTip: Use weaker pin buffers to smooth shape and control cliff.
summary: Urethane control with more core influence for players needing early blend and flatter entry.
cons: Lower carry percentage than reactive
Limited use on high-volume long patterns

name: 900 Global Harsh Reality Pearl
bestFor: Moving left when fronts hook on sport
layoutTip: Longer pin and smoother VAL help reduce corner overjump.
summary: A cleaner sport option that still creates enough angle for carry after transition.
cons: Can be too clean early in block
Needs release consistency

name: Roto Grip Gem Black
laneMatch: Long oil and high-volume challenge patterns
bowlerMatch: Higher speed and lower rev bowlers
layoutTip: Use medium layout first, then tune with 2000-3000 grit.
summary: Strong traction ball for fresh volume where most pieces skid past the breakpoint.
cons: Can burn up quickly on medium volumes
Requires cleaner follow-up options

name: Track Archetype Hybrid
layoutTip: Use benchmark pin and tune with hand position before surface changes.
summary: One of the safer benchmark choices for tournament blocks with changing blends.
cons: Not the biggest backend ball
Can be too smooth if you need angle

name: Brunswick Infinity Tour
bowlerMatch: Players with hand who need shape control
layoutTip: Smoother layout and 3000 finish keeps motion continuous.
summary: Smooth and trustworthy motion that keeps misses manageable on flatter conditions.
cons: Less pop for carry on burn
Needs defined friction to corner hard

name: Ebonite Game Breaker 5 Solid
bestFor: Tournament players who want benchmark predictability
layoutTip: Keep layout simple and tune with hand before re-surfacing.
summary: Clean benchmark read ball that keeps decisions simple during long tournament blocks.
cons: Less total hook than top asym options
Can leave corners when pattern gets steep

name: Columbia 300 Atlas Solid
bestFor: Medium-long volumes needing stronger middle read
laneMatch: Fresh tournament blocks with hold in the middle
layoutTip: Surface between 2000 and 3000 to dial in continuity.
summary: Stronger midlane option for tournament players who need oil control without quit.
cons: Too much for short patterns
Needs lane speed to avoid roll-out

name: DV8 Dark Side
bowlerMatch: Players needing cleaner look after stronger solids
layoutTip: Longer pin and polish can create needed continuation.
summary: Useful move-right-to-left transition piece for carrying corners later in blocks.
cons: Not for fresh volume
Can overreact if fronts go fast
